seo.title: Local GEO: How Local Businesses Get Recommended by AI
seo.meta_description: Local GEO explained: how local businesses get recommended by ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI Overviews using Business Profile, reviews, local pages and schema.

h1: Local GEO: How Local Businesses Get Recommended by AI Assistants
answer: Local GEO helps a local business get named when people ask AI assistants for providers nearby, such as "best accountant in Anaheim". It combines a complete Google Business Profile, steady detailed reviews, consistent name, address and phone details, real location and service pages, LocalBusiness schema, and mentions in local directories and press.
key_takeaways: People ask AI assistants for local recommendations, not just maps.
Google Business Profile and reviews feed many local answers.
Consistent name, address and phone details build trust.
Location pages need real local specifics, not swapped city names.
Local mentions and directories help assistants describe you.

sections.heading: How local searches are changing
sections.body_html:
Local questions used to mean a map pack and ten blue links. Now people also ask assistants: "who's the best wedding tent rental in Orange County?", "accountant in Anaheim who handles small business taxes". Gemini and Google AI Overviews draw on Google's local information, while ChatGPT, Perplexity and Copilot use web search results, directories and reviews.

The answer usually names a handful of businesses with short reasons. Local GEO aims to make yours one of them, described correctly.

Voice assistants and in-car systems add to this. When someone asks for a nearby provider while driving or cooking, they hear one or two names, not a list of ten. Being one of those names is the whole game.

sections.heading: Start with your Google Business Profile
sections.body_html:
• Primary category: the most specific one that fits your main service.
  • Services and products: listed in full, with short descriptions.
  • Service area and hours: accurate, including holidays.
  • Photos: real work, team and premises, updated regularly.
  • Description: a plain statement of what you do, for whom and where.
  • Questions and answers: answer common questions on the profile.

Google's own local surfaces lean on this profile heavily, and other assistants often encounter the same details through search results.

sections.heading: Reviews: volume, detail and recency
sections.body_html: AI assistants summarize what customers say. A business with many recent, detailed reviews gives them clear reasons to recommend it: "known for fast setup", "great with large events". Ask happy customers to mention the service they used and what stood out. Reply to reviews, including critical ones, calmly and specifically. Spread reviews across the platforms your customers use, not just one.

sections.heading: Location and service pages that work
sections.body_html:
1. One page per area you genuinely serve, with specifics: local projects, venues, regulations, travel times or neighborhoods.
  2. One page per core service, answering what it is, who it is for, price factors and timelines.
  3. A direct answer first on each, naming the service and area.
  4. Local proof: photos, testimonials and case examples from that area.
  5. Clear contact path: phone, form and service area on every page.

Pages that only swap the city name are thin and rarely cited.

sections.heading: Consistency and structured data
sections.body_html: Use exactly the same business name, address and phone number on your website, Business Profile, social profiles and directories. Add LocalBusiness (or a more specific subtype) schema with your name, address, phone, hours, geo coordinates and service area, matching your profile. Inconsistent details make it harder for any engine to be confident about who you are and where you work.

sections.heading: Local mentions and directories
sections.body_html:
• Chamber of commerce and local business associations.
  • Industry directories and "best of" lists for your city.
  • Local news coverage, sponsorships and community events.
  • Partner and supplier pages that link to you.

Each mention reinforces what you do and where. Assistants that search the web find these pages when answering local questions.

sections.heading: Measuring local GEO
sections.body_html: Track calls, direction requests and website clicks in your Business Profile insights, AI-referred sessions in Google Analytics 4, and form submissions by landing page. Each month, ask the main assistants your top local questions, such as service plus city, and record whether you are named and how you are described.

sections.heading: Common local GEO mistakes
sections.body_html:
• An incomplete Business Profile with a vague category, missing services or old hours.
  • Different business names on your site, profile and directories, such as abbreviations or old brand names.
  • Thin city pages that copy the same text with a different place name.
  • Reviews concentrated on one platform, or long gaps with no new reviews.
  • Hiding the service area or making customers hunt for a phone number.
  • Ignoring critical reviews instead of replying calmly with specifics.

Each of these makes it harder for an assistant to be confident about recommending you.

sections.heading: Local GEO for service-area businesses
sections.body_html: Businesses that travel to customers, such as event rentals, contractors and cleaning services, often have no storefront to anchor them on a map. For them, the service area does the work. Set it accurately in your Business Profile, list the cities you cover on a single service-area page with real examples from each, and mention travel times or minimum orders where they matter. When an assistant answers "who serves Irvine?", clear service-area details are what let it include you.

sections.heading: A 30-day local GEO plan
sections.body_html: Week one: complete your Business Profile and fix inconsistent listings. Week two: rewrite your homepage and main service page openings to name your service and area. Week three: ask your last 20 happy customers for detailed reviews. Week four: publish one strong location page with real local proof, and test your local questions in Gemini, ChatGPT and Google.

faqs.a: It is the work of getting a local business named when people ask AI assistants for nearby providers. It combines Google Business Profile, reviews, consistent business details, real location and service pages, LocalBusiness schema and local mentions.

faqs.q: Does Google Business Profile affect AI answers?
faqs.a: Google's local surfaces rely heavily on Business Profile information, and the same details often appear in the search results other assistants use. A complete, accurate profile is the foundation of local GEO.

faqs.q: How do reviews help with AI recommendations?
faqs.a: Assistants summarize what customers say. Many recent, detailed reviews give them specific reasons to recommend you and describe your strengths.

faqs.q: Do I need a page for every city?
faqs.a: Only for areas you genuinely serve, and each page needs real local specifics. Pages that only swap the city name are thin and rarely help.

faqs.q: What schema should a local business use?
faqs.a: LocalBusiness or a more specific subtype, with name, address, phone, hours, coordinates and service area that exactly match your Business Profile.

faqs.q: How do I know if local GEO is working?
faqs.a: Watch Business Profile calls and clicks, AI-referred visits and leads in Google Analytics 4, and test your service-plus-city questions in the main assistants every month.
